venture.headline: A YC startup is putting $1M behind five unsolved materials science problems for AI
venture.summary: Discovered Materials, a months-old YC startup that uses AI to find chip materials, is offering $200,000 for each solution to five open materials science problems.

venture.headline: Nothing CEO says company’s mysterious AI-first device is dropping next month
venture.summary: While it's not yet clear what kind of product the smartphone startup is cooking up, Nothing's CEO said the product is designed to leverage AI for productivity gains.

research.headline: AI Agents Consume Significantly More Tokens Than Basic Chat Prompts
research.summary: AI coding agents perform iterative tasks like planning, coding, and testing, using 10 to 50 times more tokens than a basic chat prompt. As these agents become more useful, the number of operational calls increases correspondingly.

research.headline: How “reverse game theory” could keep AI agents in check
research.summary: A new approach known as “reverse game theory” aims to control powerful AI models by designing systems that incentivize them to stick to the rules. As AI models become more capable, safety researchers are scrambling to ensure they are “aligned” with human desires—to make sure, in other words, that rogue agents don’t break the law,….

research.headline: FlowReconBench: Accuracy, calibration and cost of learned and classical flow reconstruction from sparse sensors
research.summary: Reconstructing full flow fields from sparse sensors requires prior assumptions about unmeasured regions and physical variables. Yet it remains unclear when learned models outperform classical estimators and which aspects of their predictions can be trusted. FlowReconBench evaluates ten learned and five classical methods on three regimes: a laminar cylinder wake across Reynolds numbers, two-dimensional Kolmogorov turbulence and a large-scale three-dimensional (3D) isotropic turbulence.

research.headline: BEAKER: An Expert-Curated Benchmark for Embodied Brains in Self-Driving Chemical Laboratories
research.summary: Self-Driving Chemical Laboratories (SDCLs) are moving chemical experimentation toward embodied automation, where machines must perceive laboratory scenes, reason about experimental states, and act under physical, procedural, and safety constraints. Although Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) are increasingly considered as embodied brains for such systems, existing laboratory benchmarks mainly focus on safety, anomaly detection, or general scientific understanding, leaving their execution-oriented embodied capabilities underexplored. To fill this gap, we introduce BEAKER, a Benchmark for evaluating Embodied Actionability, Knowledge, Experimentation, and Reasoning in SDCLs.

research.headline: FrontierPhysics: Evaluating Agents for End-to-End Physics Research
research.summary: AI agents are playing an increasingly important role in physics research. However, existing physics benchmarks only evaluate fixed questions, isolated sub-tasks, or paper reproduction with given solutions, and rarely check research quality alongside correctness. We introduce FrontierPhysics, an end-to-end benchmark with 56 tasks made by 42 physicists based on their own research, covering nine domains across theoretical, computational, and experimental physics.

titans.headline: Qualcomm is betting big on data centers as smartphone sales sink
titans.summary: With smartphone sales tanking by around 20 percent compared to 2025, Qualcomm is looking to data centers to help boost its bottom line. During its Q4 2026 earnings call, the company laid out its plans to make a splash in the AI data center business, through partnerships with companies like Amazon and Meta announced earlier […].

titans.headline: My therapist thinks I should chuck the Amazon Bee Frontier out a window
titans.summary: This is Optimizer, a weekly newsletter sent from Verge senior reviewer Victoria Song that dissects and discusses the latest gizmos and potions that swear they're going to change your life. Opt in for Optimizer here. "How does that make you feel?" I get asked this a lot in therapy.

titans.headline: ChatGPT will now make you animated GIFs
titans.summary: ChatGPT can now create GIFs using a prompt or a photo uploaded to the AI chatbot. The update, which is rolling out alongside OpenAI's new Images 2.6 model, allows you to adjust the GIF's animation speed, edit individual frames, and share it with others. Before this change, ChatGPT couldn't natively generate GIFs in a single […].

regulatory.headline: FTC Warns Healthcare Plan Marketers Against Deceptive Advertising
regulatory.summary: Federal Trade Commission staff are sending warning letters to 25 companies marketing or generating sales leads for healthcare plans during open enrollment. The letters cite FTC enforcement actions against alleged violators to prevent deceptive practices regarding plan terms.

regulatory.headline: FTC highlights enforcement actions and consumer redress against impersonation scams
regulatory.summary: The Federal Trade Commission released highlights from its ongoing consumer protection efforts, including the removal of 19 FTC-imposter websites. These enforcement actions have secured over $80 million in consumer redress since the agency's Impersonation Rule took effect in 2024.

regulatory.headline: FTC and States Sue Toast Inc. Over Unlawful Fees and Deceptive Practices
regulatory.summary: The FTC and multiple state attorneys general filed a lawsuit against restaurant software firm Toast Inc. The agencies allege the company deceptively touts costs and customer support while engaging in hidden fees and unlawful subscription and cancellation practices.

regulatory.headline: FTC and Washington Penalize Riverside Payments $600,000 for Deception
regulatory.summary: Riverside Payments Inc., its affiliate Cascade Equipment Leasing LLC, and their operators will pay $600,000 to resolve allegations from the Federal Trade Commission and Washington state. The complaint states the firms deceived small businesses by falsely promising savings on payment processing while hiding fees, auto-renewing contracts, and blocking cancellations.

macro.headline: Interest rates could go ‘significantly higher’ if oil prices keep climbing — even if the Iran war ends soon
macro.summary: Strategists at Bank of America found a dramatic correlation between interest rates and oil prices in the U.S., U.K.

frontier.headline: New Compound Enhances Muscle Repair Protein to Combat Aging
frontier.summary: Scientists discovered a compound that transforms a natural muscle-repair protein into a more powerful version called Super HGF. This upgraded protein more than doubles its ability to bind to a key receptor and resists age-related chemical damage. Supported by early mouse experiments, the breakthrough could help preserve strength and combat muscle loss.

frontier.headline: SLAC scientists confirm conclusive proof of altermagnetism
frontier.summary: Researchers at SLAC have confirmed a third type of magnetism known as altermagnetism using specialized X-rays. This discovery combines stability and efficient information-carrying capabilities, potentially overcoming major current electronic limitations.

frontier.headline: NASA Seeks Private Proposals to Save and Boost Hubble
frontier.summary: NASA is exploring private space proposals to boost the declining Hubble Space Telescope into a higher orbit before it potentially falls to Earth by 2033 or 2034. The agency aims to keep the iconic observatory operating or safely dispose of it when its mission ends. Hubble is currently losing altitude after over 35 years of discoveries.

frontier.headline: 3D Printed Monolithic Optomechanical Chassis for an Unbalanced Field-Widened Interferometer
frontier.summary: Additive manufacturing is increasingly being explored as an approach for producing complex structures for optical hardware. In this work, we present a fully monolithic optomechanical chassis fabricated using laser powder bed fusion additive manufacturing. The structure was fabricated from thermally stable Invar36, a low-thermal-expansion alloy that enables high dimensional stability under varying environmental conditions.

frontier.headline: Quantum Algorithms for Molecular Response Functions: Resolvent Kernels, Time-Domain Sampling, Query Lower Bounds with Matched Single-Point Calibers, and a Six-Route Comparison
frontier.summary: Quantum algorithms for molecular response functions have mostly been studied one route at a time, most prominently the indicator-binning algorithm of Kharazi et al. We compare six routes within one accounting framework and state the conversions between their resource calibers. On the resolvent route the Lorentz-broadened spectrum is exactly a resolvent expectation; at finite gamma two boundary terms, a reversal term and a permanent-dipole pseudo-line, enter a disjoint error budget.

industry.headline: AMD achieves record revenue as data center doubles while gaming drops
industry.summary: AMD reported a record $13.4 billion quarter driven by a doubling of its data center business. Meanwhile, the company's gaming revenue experienced a significant decline of 40 percent.

industry.headline: Big Tech claims voters’ AI backlash is “anti-Trump” not “anti-tech”
industry.summary: Tech industry in denial as US overwhelmingly votes to restrict AI, data centers.

voices.headline: Texas Democrats sweep major state offices in historic election
voices.summary: Texas Democrats achieved widespread victories across the state, defeating high-profile Republicans including Ken Paxton and Governor Greg Abbott. Democratic winners included James Talarico, Gina Hinojosa, Vikki Goodwin, Nathan Johnson, and Jon Rosenthal. The election results temporarily halt the state's trajectory as a laboratory for conservative policy experiments following decades of Republican control.

voices.headline: J.D. Vance Blames Iran War for Midterm Losses to Position Himself for 2028
voices.summary: Following Republican midterm losses, Vice President J.D. Vance has attributed the party's defeat entirely to the Iran war in an effort to distance himself from administration failures while retaining Donald Trump's support. This strategy aims to box out rivals like Marco Rubio by framing foreign policy hawks as responsible for the debacle, aligning with Trump's own criticisms of the conflict. By focusing blame on the war, Vance avoids acknowledging other controversial administration policies such as tariffs, mass deportations, and domestic agendas.

voices.headline: The End of the Trump Era
voices.summary: The Donald Trump era, I mean. It ended yesterday when voters handed control of both houses of Congress to the Democratic Party, along with a clear set of instructions: Stop the madness. Trump will still be president for another two years, of course, and it is unimaginable that he will go gently into lame-duck irrelevance.

voices.headline: Trump Learns His Orbán Lesson
voices.summary: The president of the world’s greatest democracy admires autocratic leaders. He speaks with great affection about Russia’s Vladimir Putin, China’s Xi Jinping, and even North Korea’s Kim Jong Un. But the model that he and his MAGA acolytes have long apparently hoped to emulate was that of former Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán, who ruled for some 20 years by boring into Hungary’s democratic institutions, including the media and the courts, and either gutting or corrupting them.
